previous.description: MCP (Model Context Protocol) server exposing Kookerella.FsOpenXmlDsl's Excel read/write/code-generation capabilities as tools any MCP-compatible AI agent can call directly - build a workbook, read one back, or decompile an existing one into idiomatic, runnable F# or C# source, without the agent needing to write any F# or C# itself. Unlike libraries that only build or mutate a workbook through an imperative API, this can translate an existing .xlsx/.xlsm back into source that reproduces it. The same translation is available as a plain CLI (fsopenxmldsl-mcp convert file.xlsx --lang csharp) for anyone not going through an MCP client.

current.description: MCP (Model Context Protocol) server exposing Kookerella.FsOpenXmlDsl's Excel capabilities as tools any MCP-compatible AI agent can call directly: build a workbook, read one back, decompile an existing one into idiomatic F# or C# source, or translate to/from plain XML against a real embedded schema. The XML direction has two uses beyond code generation: build an .xlsx directly from XML a transform engine (e.g. XSLT) already produces, no code required; or convert an existing .xlsx to XML for text-based diffing and version control in systems like git, with deterministically ordered output so real content changes stay isolated in the diff. The same conversions are available as plain CLI commands (fsopenxmldsl-mcp convert/build) for anyone not going through an MCP client.

previous.description: A cross-branch state cache for Git repositories. Answers, for a set of paths, which monitored branches carry changes a client does not have and what content they carry, using only git over HTTPS so it behaves identically against GitHub and Azure DevOps. Maintains a bare blobless mirror per repository, serves blob ids from a merge-base keyed diff cache, and performs every upstream operation with the requesting client's own credential. Ships as a dotnet tool and as a container image for Kubernetes.

previous.description: A caching reverse proxy for the Git LFS HTTP API. Relays every Batch API call upstream so upstream remains the sole authority on access, rewrites the returned transfer URLs to point at itself, and serves object bytes from a local content-addressed store.
